items.title: [@payloadcms/storage-vercel-blob] @payloadcms/storage-vercel-blob has access control bypass of uploads in Vercel Storage adapter
items.summary: ImpactIn affected configurations, client upload access does not consistently align with the associated collection’s access configuration.You are affected if:You use client uploads with @payloadcms/storage-vercel-blob.Authenticated users can access the client-upload route.Applications that do not enable client uploads are not affected.PatchesClient uploads now require authentication and the appropriate collection-level access before upload access is granted.Users should upgrade Payload packages to >= 3.90.0 or >= 4.0.0-canary.34.WorkaroundsUpgrading to a patched version is recommended. Until you can upgrade, disable client uploads or configure the upload route’s access control to enforce the associated collection’s permissions.Referenceshttps://github.com/payloadcms/payload/security/advisories/GHSA-mc8m-rr6c-r5qrhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-93363https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/commit/47abe9bb5c444330dbfaa9a5bc2033337932270bhttps://github.com/payloadcms/payload/releases/tag/v3.90.0https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/payload-cms-storage-vercel-blob-adapter-improper-access-control-on-upload-routehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mc8m-rr6c-r5qr

items.title: [odf-kit] odf-kit: HTML injection leading to XSS in odtToHtml() and odsToHtml() via unescaped style attribute values
items.summary: SummaryODF style attribute values are interpolated into style="..." attributes without HTML-escaping in both of odf-kit's to-HTML renderers (odtToHtml and odsToHtml). A double-quote character inside an attacker-controlled style value breaks out of the attribute, allowing arbitrary HTML/attribute injection — and therefore script execution (XSS) — from a crafted .odt or .ods file wherever the rendered output is inserted as HTML, which is the documented purpose of both functions.DetailsODT renderer (src/odt/to-html/html-renderer.ts)The renderer has an escapeHtml() helper and applies it consistently to text content and to attribute values — href, src, alt, id, data-author, data-date, citation text all go through it. The inline CSS strings do not.In renderTextSpan (dist/odt/to-html/html-renderer.js:195):const css = spanStyleToCss(span.style);if (css) html = `${html}`;The value of e.g. fo:color is copied from the document into style.fontColor verbatim by the parser (extractSpanStyle, read/parser.js:348), then concatenated raw into the attribute. A " in the value terminates the attribute early.The same unescaped style="${...}" pattern appears at roughly ten other emission sites: paragraph and heading (paragraphStyleToCss), table cells and rows (cellStyleToCss, rowStyleToCss), , and the image style attribute. The affected source attributes include fo:color, fo:background-color, fo:text-shadow, fo:letter-spacing, fo:font-family (via both direct and font-face resolution), fo:margin-*, fo:padding-*, fo:line-height, fo:border*, and style:vertical-align.ODS renderer (src/ods/to-html/html-renderer.ts) — same bugbuildInlineStyle() assembles the CSS string from cell formatting properties — fo:color, fo:font-size, fo:font-family, fo:background-color, fo:text-align, etc. — with zero escapeHtml calls, and renderCell emits it raw (line 65):if (includeStyles && cell.formatting) { const style = buildInlineStyle(cell.formatting); if (style) attrs.push(`style="${style}"`);}Additionally, row.height (from style:row-height) goes raw into the row element (line 95):const style = includeStyles && row.height ? ` style="height:${row.height}"` : "";return `${cells}`;The same injection is reachable through the public odf-kit/ods/to-html export (odsToHtml()), so both to-HTML directions are affected.Version scopeThe odt/to-html and ods/to-html modules first shipped in 0.14.0; the current latest release is 0.14.1. The PoCs were re-ran against the unreleased main branch (commit 270a361) — both injections still fire, so no fix has landed past the release.PoCEach PoC is a minimal ODF package (mimetype + META-INF/manifest.xml + content.xml) whose content.xml contains exactly one poisoned automatic style. The files are generated by this short Python script (stdlib only, no dependencies) — save as build-pocs.py and run python3 build-pocs.py:import zipfiledef build(path, mimetype, content): # ODF requires 'mimetype' first and stored uncompressed with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as z: z.writestr(zipfile.ZipInfo("mimetype"), mimetype, compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_STORED) z.writestr("META-INF/manifest.xml", ' ' ' ' ' ' ' ' ' ') z.writestr("content.xml", content)ODT = "application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text"ODS = "application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet"HEAD = (' ' '')Q = """p1 = f"red{Q} onmouseover={Q}alert(1){Q} x={Q}" # attribute injectionp2 = f'red{Q}><img src=x onerror={Q}alert(1){Q}><x style={Q}' # full markup injection# .odt: one paragraph with a poisoned automatic text styledef odt(p): return (HEAD + ' ' ' ' f' ' ' ' 'hello' ' ')# .ods: one cell with a poisoned automatic cell styledef ods(p): return (HEAD + ' ' ' '
